answer: select avg(n) from (select b.c0000, count(*) n from t0001 b join t0002 m on m.c0000=b.c0000 where m.c0001='+' and b.c0001='-' group by 1)
select sum(a.c0000='i') as iodine, sum(a.c0000='s') as sulfur from t0003 a where a.c0001 in (select c.c0002 from t0000 c join t0001 b on b.c0002=c.c0001 where b.c0001='-')
select count(*) from t0003 where c0002 in (select c0000 from t0001 where c0001='#') and c0002 in (select c0002 from t0003 where c0000 in ('p','br'))

select a.c0002 as molecule_id, count(c.c0001) as bond_count from t0003 a left join t0000 c on c.c0002=a.c0001 where a.c0000 in (select c0000 from t0003 group by 1 having count(distinct c0002)=1) and a.c0002 in (select c0000 from t0002 where c0001='+') group by 1 order by 1
select round(1.0*(select count(*) from t0000 c join t0003 a on a.c0001=c.c0002 where a.c0002='TR397')/(select count(*) from t0003 where c0002='TR397'),2)

select a.c0000, count(*) from t0003 a where exists(select 1 from t0000 c join t0001 b on b.c0002=c.c0001 where c.c0002=a.c0001 and b.c0001='-') and not exists(select 1 from t0000 c join t0001 b on b.c0002=c.c0001 where c.c0002=a.c0001 and b.c0001<>'-') group by 1 order by 1
